transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, hi. Thank you for seeing me. I, uh... I guess I'm here because I haven't been feeling quite like myself lately. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know people have it worse, but... most days, it just feels like I'm sitting at the bottom of a really dark hole. 

Even when I'm at work, or around people I've known for years, I just... I can't seem to shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. I try to put on a brave face, I really do, but it's just so heavy. Is... is that the kind of thing you need to know? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in them?

Well, um... maybe a little bit? I really don't want to sound lazy, because I've always been a hard worker, but... yeah. 

I used to really love being active. Hiking, painting... even just tinkering around at the local makerspace. I used to actually enjoy figuring out a tricky install at work, too. But lately... I don't know. I just kind of stare at my supplies. And when people call to see if I want to go do something, I've just been... ignoring them. 

I feel terrible admitting that, I really do. It's just that none of it feels worth starting right now. I'm sorry, I know that sounds awful, and I really am trying to push myself to get back into things. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope that makes sense.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently? Like eating significantly less or losing weight without trying?

Um, well... I guess maybe my eating has been a little off lately. I mean, I don't want you to think I'm not taking care of myself, because I know how important nutrition is, but... it's just been a bit erratic, I suppose. 

During the day, I mostly just run on coffee. It's not that I'm trying to starve myself or anything, it's just that the thought of food kind of... turns my stomach, I guess? But then late at night, I find myself just sort of picking at whatever's in the cabinet. I don't even really taste it, to be honest. 

I know I should be eating better, regular meals and all that. I'm really trying to get back on a normal schedule. Does... does that happen sometimes with people? I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than it is.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these feelings been present most days, and have they lasted throughout the day?

Um... well, it's been a while, I guess. I mean, I really didn't want to bother anyone about it, because I kept thinking I could just push through it and snap out of it on my own. I know people get sad sometimes, right? 

But, um... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope this doesn't make me sound weak or anything... it's been about a year and two months. Ever since... well, I had this fall at an HVAC job I was working on, and it left me with a bad back injury. After that, it just felt like everything started unraveling, you know? 

And as for how often... yeah, it's pretty much most days. And it just kind of sits there all day long. I really try my best to shake it off, I promise I do, but it just won't lift. Is... is it normal for it to last that long after something like an injury? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, have you felt restless or unable to sit still?

Um... well, I really try to keep my pace up, I promise. I know how frustrating it is to be around someone who's dragging their feet, especially when you're used to working fast. But... um... I guess I have been a little sluggish lately. 

It's actually really embarrassing to admit, but it feels like everything I do is just... slow now. Even just simple things, like getting from the couch to the kitchen, it takes me so much longer than it should. Or... or even right now, sometimes answering a simple question just takes me a minute to process and get the words out. I'm really sorry if I'm taking up too much of your time with my pauses. 

People have started noticing, too, which makes me feel awful for worrying them. They keep asking if I'm okay, and they say I look like I'm moving like I'm underwater. I really am trying my hardest to move normally and be present, I swear. Is... is that slowness something you see in other people? Am I explaining that okay?
Have you ever felt so overwhelmed or hopeless that you've thought about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Oh... um. That's... that's a hard question. I really don't want you to think I'm crazy, or that I'm not grateful for the life I have. I know I have a lot to be thankful for, and I really do try to focus on the positive, I promise. 

But... um... sometimes, when the back pain is just so bad, and I'm sitting there worrying about how I'm going to pay the bills since I can't work... my mind goes to some pretty dark places. I guess I've had these thoughts lately that... well, that maybe everyone would just be better off if I didn't wake up in the morning. Like I wouldn't be a burden anymore. 

And, um... I hate to even say this out loud, because it scares me so much, but... sometimes I actually catch myself thinking about just ending it. I don't want to, really I don't, and I'm trying so hard to fight it. Please tell me you don't think I'm a terrible person for having those thoughts. Is that... is that something you can help me with?
Have you ever experienced a period like this before, where you felt persistently down and lost interest in things, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

Um... well, no, I don't think so. I really don't want to take up too much of your time with my past, but... I've always tried to be a pretty upbeat person, you know? I've always worked hard and just kept moving forward. 

So, um... yeah, this is really the first time I've ever felt anything like this. I've never been one to just sit around and feel sorry for myself, I promise. I always thought I was pretty strong before the accident. 

I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than I should be. Is it... is it okay that this is the first time it's happened? Am I giving you the right kind of answers?
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually high, extremely energetic, or so irritable that people noticed and said you were not your usual self?

Oh, um... no. I don't think I've ever felt like that. I hope it's okay to just say no to that one... I really want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information. 

But, um, I've never really been the type to get super hyper or, you know, fly off the handle at people. Even back when I was working full-time doing repairs, I always just tried to keep my head down, be steady, and get along with everyone. I really pride myself on being level-headed. I promise I've never had a time where I was acting out of control or anything like that. 

Is... is that a good thing? I just really hope I'm answering these questions the way you need me to.
Have you ever had any other times in your life when you felt persistently down, lost interest in things, or experienced similar symptoms, even if it was less severe or didn’t last as long?

Um... no, I really don't think so. I know we kind of just touched on that, and I hope I'm not being difficult by just giving you the exact same answer again. I really am trying to think back carefully for you, I promise. 

But... honestly, even just feeling a little bit down for a few days, I never really let myself get stuck there in the past. If I had a bad day, I'd just go to work, focus on my repair jobs, and make sure to keep a smile on my face. I've always tried to be the person who lifts other people up, you know? Not the one complaining or bringing the mood down. 

So, no, nothing even mild like this before the accident. I hope... I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm being as helpful as I can be, and that I'm giving you all the right details.
